basis: Craniosynostosis and cataract are the defining skeletal and ocular abnormalities; further phenotypic information is unavailable.
Aldosterone synthesis deficiency causes electrolyte imbalance and salt wasting; renal structural disease is not established.
PTH resistance defines an endocrine disorder; hypocalcemic seizures are metabolic manifestations without established lasting neurologic damage.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disease presenting as infantile encephalomyopathy defines metabolic, brain and skeletal-muscle involvement.
Inherited cardiac rhythm disorder with atrial fibrillation in all 21 annotated patients.
Familial bipolar affective disorder with mania and depression; purely psychiatric disease has no axis.
Isolated sperm formation and motility defects causing male infertility; reproductive function is outside the axes.
Split-hand/split-foot malformations and congenital ocular abnormalities, especially nystagmus, define the syndrome.
Intellectual disability and epilepsy define neurologic disease; dental anomalies define gastrointestinal involvement because teeth belong to that axis.
Retinal vascular and vitreoretinal disease; the broader CTNNB1 parent does not establish neurodevelopmental impairment in this specific subtype.
Congenital titin myopathy causes weakness, contractures and fractures; cardiac abnormalities are explicitly part of the defining phenotype.
Inherited tryptophan metabolism disorder characterized by intellectual disability; frequencies of additional skeletal, ocular and hearing abnormalities are unclear.
Meningioma arising in the falx cerebri is a central nervous system meningeal tumour.
Defining bradykinin-mediated edema affects subcutaneous tissue, bowel and upper airway; F12-related angioedema is not an autoimmune or coagulation-deficiency disorder.
Salmonella infection directly inflames the gastrointestinal tract.
Follicular ichthyosis is a cutaneous keratinization disorder; no syndromic extracutaneous features are established here.
Cryoglobulin-mediated peripheral nerve injury, typically through immune-complex mechanisms; other systemic cryoglobulinemic lesions are not assumed.
Joint instability, osteopenia and skin fragility define the syndrome; structural mitral valve prolapse occurs in 4/6 annotated patients.
Bone fragility defines OI; dentinogenesis imperfecta occurs in 1/1 annotated patient. Blue sclerae are nondamaging; kidney stones are separate; lung-damage frequency is unclear.
Immune-mediated vasculitis confined to CNS vessels, with frequent cerebral infarction, white-matter injury and neurologic deficits.
Paralysis of pupillary and accommodation functions; the oculomotor-nerve-paralysis parent establishes associated neural dysfunction.
Glucocorticoid resistance causes endocrine and electrolyte abnormalities; hormone-driven hypertension occurs in 30-79%. Hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.
Defined by atrial septal defect together with acquired mitral stenosis; both are cardiac structural abnormalities.
Molar-root abnormalities and taurodontism are consistent defining findings; glaucoma and hypotrichosis are variable, without established frequency of at least 30%.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define the syndrome; esotropia affects 4/18 in the full cohort despite selected 4/4 reports. Feeding support does not establish GI damage.
